_why: ADR 0119's table. A plain-language question can now name the system, and
these are the ways that could turn into SILENT inference -- which is the
one thing the constraint it relaxes exists to prevent.
Every mutation here attacks the same property: a real BRENDA citation
must never be attached to a system no person confirmed.

mutations.description: a bare return counts as consent
_note: The default flips from no to yes. An empty line is somebody pressing
return to make a prompt go away, and reading it as agreement makes
the confirmation decorative -- present in review, functionally a
silent inference.
This is the likeliest careless change: `answer !== 'n'` reads as
friendlier and is the bug.

mutations.description: a headless run auto-confirms instead of refusing
_note: With no terminal there is nobody to ask. A default-confirm here is
exactly the inference the constraint forbids, with a prompt in the
code path that nobody ever sees -- a pipe, a CI job or `| head`
would silently attach citations to a parsed system.
It would also look correct in every interactive test, because those
have a TTY.
`--yes` skips the QUESTION, not the DISCLOSURE. A batch run whose
citations came from a parse has to say so in its own transcript, or
nobody can audit afterwards which system was actually cited.
Deleting the write is the tempting tidy-up: the prompt is skipped,
so the text looks like leftovers.

mutations.description: the parser stops refusing a question that names nothing
_note: `plausible()` rejects a fragment made entirely of noise words, so
'of the model on the model in the model' matches the SHAPE and still
returns null. Without it the tool would offer a command naming
'model' as an enzyme, which discredits every suggestion it makes.
A wrong suggestion is worse than none: it teaches a student the tool
guesses badly, and they stop reading the ones that are right.
mutations._verdict: NOT CAUGHT -- and the verdict is WRONG. See _y4_is_a_harness_finding.

_why_one_file_and_what_that_costs: Y1-Y3 mutate `confirmSystem.ts`, whose tests are all in this one file.
Y4 mutates `suggestResolveCommand.ts` and is run against ITS file, with
`--test` overridden on the command line -- recorded here rather than
left as an undocumented second invocation:
Both files in one command is the correct default and it does not fit:
baseline plus one mutation exceeded the 178 s per-call ceiling in this
environment (measured -- the run was interrupted mid-Y1). Splitting the
RUN without splitting the RECORD is what --only is for (ADR 0083); this
note exists so the narrower command is not mistaken for the ADR 0026
mistake, where a set ran a suite narrower than the record cited and
_y4_is_a_harness_finding: Y4 came back NOT CAUGHT, and it should have been caught. Direct
execution of the mutated module settles it:
under mutation -> {"enzyme":"model","substrate":"model",
"organism":"model"}
The test asserts `toBeNull()` on that exact query, so it MUST fail. Jest
reported 15 of 15 passing.
So the behaviour changed, the assertion covers it, and the runner did
not see the change -- which is ADR 0083 verbatim: a JavaScript runner's
transform cache manufacturing a false NOT CAUGHT. `--no-cache` was
passed twice here (injected by mutate.py, and again in --test) and did
not prevent it.
NOT-YET-REPRODUCIBLE.txt records ADR 0083's fix as 'reasoned and
harmless, and unproven for the case it was written for', because the
confirming run did not fit the ceiling. This is that case, reproduced,
and it says the fix is NOT sufficient.
The asymmetry from ADR 0083 still holds and is why the other three
verdicts stand: a stale cache can only manufacture a false NOT CAUGHT,
never a false 'caught'. Y1, Y2 and Y3 were caught, and a cache cannot
produce that.
Y4's PROPERTY is verified -- by direct execution, printed above -- but
not by this harness. Recorded as unverified-by-mutation rather than
claimed as caught, because a verdict the harness never established is
the thing this whole directory exists to prevent.
